name: Air temperature
definition: How warm the air is two metres above the ground, averaged over the month.

name: Maximum temperature
definition: The highest hourly air temperature two metres above the ground during the month.

name: Minimum temperature
definition: The lowest hourly air temperature two metres above the ground during the month.

name: Surface (skin) temperature
definition: How warm the very top of the ground or of the sea is, averaged over the month. Over open sea this is the sea-surface temperature, which the model is given rather than calculates.

name: Precipitation
definition: How much rain and snow falls, given as the average amount per day over the month.
trend_note: Rainfall trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Relative humidity
definition: How close the air two metres above the ground is to being saturated with water vapour, as a percentage, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Humidity trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Specific humidity
definition: How many grams of water vapour each kilogram of air two metres above the ground holds, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Humidity trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Wind speed at 10 m
definition: How fast the wind blows ten metres above the ground, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Wind trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Surface soil wetness
definition: How wet the top 5 cm of soil is, from 0 for completely dry to 1 for completely soaked, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Soil wetness is calculated by the model from its own rainfall, so its trends are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Root-zone soil wetness
definition: How wet the soil is down to where plant roots reach, from 0 for completely dry to 1 for completely soaked, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Soil wetness is calculated by the model from its own rainfall, so its trends are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Sunlight reaching the surface
definition: How much energy from sunlight reaches flat ground each day, counting cloudy days, averaged over the month.
source: NASA POWER (GEWEX SRB to 2000, CERES from 2001)

name: Cloud cover
definition: How much of the sky is covered by cloud, as a percentage, averaged over the month.
source: NASA POWER (GEWEX SRB to 2000, CERES from 2001)

name: Snow depth
definition: How deep the snow lying on the ground is, averaged over the month. Snow-free land reads zero, and over open sea POWER has no value.
trend_note: Snow trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Snowfall
definition: How much snow falls on land, given as the average amount of melted water per day over the month. Snow-free land reads zero, and over open sea POWER has no value.
trend_note: Snow trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Snow cover
definition: How much of the land is covered by snow, from 0 for none to 1 for all of it, averaged over the month. Snow-free land reads zero, and over open sea POWER has no value.
trend_note: Snow trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Sea ice
definition: How much of the sea in the grid cell is covered by ice, from 0 for open water to 1 for full cover, averaged over the month. Inland places and seas that never freeze read zero.
trend_note: The model takes sea ice from satellite-based ocean analyses. Near Helsinki and Longyearbyen the record shows ice in months that should be ice-free until about 2005 and steps down in 2005 to 2007, so a trend or record year can be an artefact of the data, not a change in the ice.

name: Surface air pressure
definition: The pressure of the air at the height of the ground in the grid cell, averaged over the month. It is lower on high ground, so it differs from the pressure on a weather map.

name: Water vapour in the air column
definition: How much water vapour the whole column of air above the ground holds, as kilograms over each square metre, averaged over the month.
trend_note: Water vapour trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Strongest wind
definition: The highest hourly wind speed ten metres above the ground in each month; a yearly value averages the months' highest winds. It is not a count of storms.
trend_note: Wind trends from this model are less reliable than temperature trends.

name: Haze
definition: How much dust, smoke and other particles in the air dim the sunlight, as aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, averaged over the month: 0 is perfectly clear and 1 is very hazy. It comes from CERES SYN1deg, which blends MODIS satellite aerosol data into a model, not from the MODIS Aqua product shown in Giovanni.
trend_note: POWER documents no change of source for haze since 2001, but changes in the satellite data its model takes in could not be ruled out.
